title: The snapshot scanner's `DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK = 25000000` is an undocumented correctness horizon for the migrate() user list

description:
The snapshot scanner's `DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK = 25000000` is an undocumented correctness horizon for the migrate() user list

Classification basis (verbatim from the severity-classifier): Low under C4: no assets at risk today and the enumeration was verified complete at the pin block; the defect is a latent correctness dependency on an undocumented constant plus a fail-open reconciliation check. Retained rather than dropped because the root cause is in committed code and the failure mode is silent.
impact: Latent, none realised. Under-enumeration would strand a user's staked position on V1 - the same end state as L-01, reached by an orthogonal route. Recoverable by owner action.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. `const DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK = 25000000n` bounds the `Staked`/`Unstaked`/`DepositedFor` log scan that produces Phase 6's `migrate()` user list.

2. Any position opened before block 25,000,000 yields a SHORT list unless `FROM_BLOCK` is overridden. Neither the story, the script NatSpec, nor the (absent) npm annotation records that this constant is load-bearing for migration completeness.
3. The TOTAL-miss case is guarded: `die(4, ...)` fires when `totalStaked > 0` but zero holders were found (:242-243).

4. The PARTIAL-miss case is not: `sumStaked != totalStaked` emits a non-fatal WARNING to stdout only (:245-248), so a partial under-enumeration still emits a snapshot that the Foundry script then trusts.
recommendation: Promote the `sumStaked !== totalStaked` warning at `:245-248` to a hard `die(4, ...)`: a list that does not reconcile against `totalStaked` is exactly the subset case the header says to avoid, and `migrate` being re-runnable makes a false abort cheap while a silent subset is expensive. Additionally, document `DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK` as 'must precede the earliest of the three stakers' deployment blocks' and record those three block numbers in the comment so the constant can be audited rather than trusted.
recommendationQuality: strong - a one-line change that converts a silent subset into a refusal
justification: Low under C4: no assets at risk today and the enumeration was verified complete at the pin block; the defect is a latent correctness dependency on an undocumented constant plus a fail-open reconciliation check. Retained rather than dropped because the root cause is in committed code and the failure mode is silent.

classification.likelihood: nil today, verified rather than assumed - the run at the pin block reconciled EXACTLY on all three stakers (1 user / sum 2 == totalStaked 2; 2 users / 146 == 146; 3 users / 13 == 13), so the horizon is currently sufficient and the emitted list is provably complete.
classification.assumptions: A staker position predating block 25,000,000, or a future staker deployment whose history precedes the constant.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the above; the operator would see a stdout warning and could miss it.

pocNote: No standalone PoC. Evidence is the run-22 mainnet-fork PREVIEW execution of `promotion-ready:dry` at block 25659373 (see the script-audit review artifacts).

severityDebate.whyRetained: The C4 'speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause' carve-out does not apply: the root cause is present in committed code (an undocumented magic number governing a safety-critical enumeration, with the partial-miss case degrading to a non-fatal warning the downstream Foundry script trusts). That it is empirically clean today is CONFIDENCE, not absence of root cause, and under Law 1 confidence never justifies a drop.
severityDebate.orderingNote: Ranked L-06 rather than lower because it carries the cheapest structural improvement in the whole set - see the report note below.

reportEmphasisPreserved: PR-04's ask (promote the `sumStaked !== totalStaked` warning at :245-248 to a hard die(4)) is the single cheapest structural improvement in the whole candidate set: it converts the silent-subset case into a refusal, and `migrate` being re-runnable makes a false abort nearly free. Worth surfacing in the report even though the severity is Low.
